thread:
maya: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we still need to decide the dequant fusion ordering for attention path when we have mixed precision (FP8/INT8/INT4). question: do we prioritize single-copy in-place dequant -> fused-attn vs explicit dequant -> generic-attn?

jonathan: my take: in-place fusion wins on latency for short sequences but hurts memory layout compatibility with KV cache replicas. also harder to fallback to fp32 kernels.

liam: +1. empirical: on A100 we saw ~8-12% p99 win for 128-512 seq with in-place. but on MI250 it was smaller, and copy-free path caused awkward 64B alignment constraints.

maya: that's the tradeoff. we need an interface that can express both without huge code duplication. proposal: kernel_selector.add_variant(name, predicate, attrs) where attrs can include "requires_aligned_kv", "dequant_mode":"inplace|copy|lazy" and an approximate perf score.

sophia: can we add a runtime hint for rollout: "prefer_stable_memory_layout": true for Dedicated/private customers? some enterprise customers rely on exact KV layout for 3rd-party tooling.

jonathan: yes, add a policy flag to routing layer. if prefer_stable_memory_layout -> force copy-dequant variant. otherwise choose by perf score + hardware capabilities.

liam: small nit: how do we handle mixed-quant batches (some tensors INT8, some FP8)? do we call two different kernels or one kernel that branches? branching in kernel kills throughput.

maya: good point. suggestion: at request-merge time we split batches by quant-type and route to specialized pools. that keeps kernels simple and allows separate batching heuristics. needs changes in our batching router.

jonathan: sounds reasonable. we should also expose a "kv_stride" contract from runtime -> model adapter so model configs can assert alignment (e.g., kv_stride % 64 == 0).

liam: here's a tiny pseudocode for selector logic I sketched:\n```\nbest = None\nfor variant in registry[op]:\n  if not variant.predicate(hw, dtype, seq, kv_layout): continue\n  score = variant.base_score * hw_perf_factor(hw) - penalty_for_unaligned(kv_layout, variant)\n  if best is None or score > best.score: best = variant\nreturn best\n```\n
sophia: can infra-bot run a quick smoke with the prototype? focus: 1) p50/p95 for seq 64/256/1024, 2) mem usage for kv cache, 3) fallback correctness to fp32.

infra-bot: build/ci pipeline kicked off for branch `quant-select-prototype`. smoke tests queued. :gear:

maya: plan for rollout: 1) land selector + variant registry behind feature-flag, 2) run canary on Dedicated region with conservative default (copy-dequant), 3) enable perf-prefers on hosted for small sequences only, 4) when stable promote to default.

jonathan: one more thing: telemetry. we need counters: chosen_variant, fallback_count, kv_alignment_mismatch. put them in our trace span for requests.

liam: i'll prototype the registry and add a small benchmark harness. will push results in a follow-up thread.

maya: thanks — gonna add tasks to the RFC TODO: registry API, batching split, rollout flags, telemetry. tagging @sophia for enterprise constraints doc.

sophia: got it. i'll draft an addendum describing allowed KV layout changes for Private deployments.

maya: wrap-up: consensus to support both in-place and copy dequant variants; selector + policy flags to decide; batching split for mixed-quant; telemetry and canary rollout.

jonathan: +1 :thumbsup:

liam: +1, will follow up with numbers.

infra-bot: smoke tests passed on small set (seq=64/256), full perf run scheduled at 2026-03-21T02:00:00Z.
